draws.name: Big-game draw — deer, elk, pronghorn, bighorn sheep (also oryx, ibex, Barbary sheep, javelina)
draws.quote: Mar 18, 2026: Deadline to apply for draw licenses for Barbary sheep, bighorn sheep, deer, elk, ibex, javelina, pronghorn, oryx and private-land only deer ... Applications must be completed before 5 p.m. Mountain Daylight Time (MDT). ... April 22, 2026: Big-game draw results are available online

fees.quote: All draw license fees include a nonrefundable application fee (residents: $7; non-residents: $13).

fees.notes: Resident game-hunting & fishing license is $42; junior game-hunting $10; senior/disabled $15.

fees.label: Nonresident game-hunting license
fees.notes: Nonresident junior game-hunting license $20. The 4-day temporary license does not allow big-game licenses.

fees.quote: Habitat Stamp* $10 $10 * Mandatory for hunting and fishing on federal U.S. Forest Service or BLM lands.

prerequisites.text: Buy a nonrefundable game-hunting (or game-hunting & fishing) license plus the Habitat Management and Access Validation (age 18+) as the first step of the online application.
prerequisites.quote: Applicants for big-game draw licenses must first select a nonrefundable Game Hunting or Game Hunting and Fishing license with a Habitat Management and Access Validation (age 18 and older only for HMAV) before they can proceed to the application process.

prerequisites.text: Pay the full license fee plus the application fee when you apply; the license fee is refunded if you are not drawn.
prerequisites.quote: The nonrefundable application fee and full license fee for each species will be charged at the time the application is submitted.

prerequisites.text: Hunters 17 and younger need a hunter education or mentor-youth number before buying the game-hunting license.
prerequisites.quote: All youth hunters, younger than 18, must have a Hunter Education certification number from New Mexico or another state, or a Mentor Youth number prior to purchasing their Game-hunting License

prerequisites.text: If you held a deer, elk, pronghorn or turkey license last year, you must file the harvest report by the draw deadline (Feb. 15 to avoid an $8 late fee), or all draw applications are rejected.
prerequisites.quote: All 2025–26 license holders must report to be eligible for 2026–27 draw licenses. ... Failure to report for these species by this date will result in rejection of all draw applications .

prerequisites.text: Nonresidents cannot apply for antlerless elk or hunts only on Wildlife Management Areas.
prerequisites.quote: Only New Mexico residents are eligible to apply for Antlerless (A) Elk Draw Licenses and hunts held exclusively on State Game Commission owned Wildlife Management Areas (WMAs).

notes: The New Mexico Department of Wildlife (formerly NMDGF) has posted 2027–28 fee schedules but no 2027 draw dates (checked 2026-11-04). The applications page and the 2026–27 rules booklet show only the 2026 cycle, so the draw is recorded with 2026 dates, marked last_year. Neither source gives an application opening date. Fees come from the 2027–28 PDFs; the 2026–27 schedule is identical. New Mexico has no preference or bonus points, so there is no point-only purchase (pointOnly is empty). Draw quotas: at least 84% of licenses go to residents, 10% to applicants using a registered NM outfitter and 6% to nonresidents without one. NM has no moose or mountain goat draw. Bear and turkey use a separate draw (deadline Feb. 11, 2026), outside this file's scope. Oryx, ibex, Barbary sheep and javelina share the main draw but have no species key here.
